candidates.title: Log sanitization — home/username forms incomplete (8.3 and short-name residuals)
candidates.rationale: redact_user_home calls redact_home_all_forms for USERPROFILE, HOME, and dirs::home_dir() with three separator forms (raw backslash, doubled-backslash, forward-slash). The function never extracts or redacts the bare username token itself, 8.3 short names (e.g. C:\Users\ALEXAN~1), or HOMEPATH-derived tails. The comment at line 207-212 explicitly documents the doubled-backslash gap was caught live (2026-06-27). The 8.3 gap is acknowledged as a conscious residual in the report's own text. However, the practical severity is low: the diagnostic report is the only consumer (build_diag_report at line 314, collect_redacted_log at line 737), and the home path itself is redacted — only obscure variant representations leak.
candidates.counterevidence: collect_redacted_log (line 737) chains redact_secrets(redact_user_home(redact_ipv4(redact_urls()))) applying all four redaction layers. The three-form masking covers the overwhelming majority of real paths. Tests at lines 820-850 verify doubled-backslash and forward-slash forms.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify whether Windows 8.3 short names actually appear in overlay-host.log or diagnostic output in practice
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `redact_home_all_forms` / `redact_home_in` (`diagnostics.rs`) only substitute the literal `USERPROFILE`/`HOME`/`dirs::home_dir()` string in three separator spellings (raw, `\\` doubled, `/`). They never redact the username token itself, 8.3 short names, or drive-less/`HOMEPATH` tails. The 8.3 gap is even documented as a “conscious residual” on `redact_home_all_forms`.

candidates.title: IPv6 / DNS host not redacted by redact_ipv4
candidates.rationale: Report claims redact_ipv4 misses IPv6 and DNS hostnames. While literally true for redact_ipv4 alone, the report fails to account for redact_urls (lines 110-141) which masks the HOST of every http(s):// URL including DNS hosts, IPv6 literals, and Tailscale/mDNS FQDNs. Tests at lines 860-880 verify IPv6 bracketed addresses and DNS hosts are masked. The redaction pipeline in both build_diag_report and collect_redacted_log applies redact_urls, making the claimed gap non-existent in practice.
candidates.counterevidence: redact_urls (line 117) masks all URL hosts including DNS and IPv6. Tests explicitly verify http://[2001:db8::1]:9000/v1 → http://***:9000/v1 and DNS hosts. The diagnostic pipeline always applies both redact_urls AND redact_ipv4.
candidates.remaining_check: None — structurally rejected
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `redact_urls` only finds case-insensitive `http://` / `https://` runs up to ASCII whitespace, then calls `mask_host`. Tests show userinfo in *http(s)* URLs is collapsed to `***`, but (a) query/fragment are kept with the path, (b) non-http URLs are untouched, (c) scheme-less hosts/IPv6 are not URLs. `redact_ipv4` is dotted-quad only. `collect_redacted_log` applies `redact_urls` → `redact_ipv4` → `redact_user_home` → `redact_secrets` (order differs from `build_diag_report`).

candidates.title: Vision capture BGRA data retained in RAM after tile closes
candidates.rationale: bgra_to_slint_image at line 51 creates a Slint SharedPixelBuffer from the raw BGRA data. The buffer is moved into the tile's Image property via Slint. When the tile closes, the Slint window is dropped and the Image/buffer should be freed. However, a detailed lifecycle analysis of Slint's refcounting is needed to confirm no references are retained. The report's claim is plausible but speculative — it asserts retention without evidence of actual retention mechanics.
candidates.counterevidence: Slint Image uses SharedPixelBuffer with reference counting. When the tile window is closed/dropped and no other references exist, the buffer is freed. No explicit BGRA storage outside the tile's Image property is visible in the code.
candidates.remaining_check: Memory profiling of a vision tile lifecycle would be needed to confirm or reject
candidates.original_candidate_title: 3. Secret token redaction — missing prefixes and brittle matching
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `redact_secrets` only matches exact `"Bearer "` (capital B, single 0x20), `"gsk_"`, and `"sk-"` with an alnum/`_` lookbehind. There is no `ghp_` / `gho_` / `github_pat_` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `hf_` / `xai-` handling. `BEARER`, `bearer`, `Bearer\t`, `Bearer:`, and `Bearer  ` (two spaces) miss. Double-space is a skip bug: after consuming `"Bearer "`, `find(char::is_whitespace)` returns 0, so the real token is left in `rest`.

candidates.title: Clipboard text retained in LAST_CLOSED_READ_TILE after read-aloud tile closes
candidates.rationale: LAST_CLOSED_READ_TILE is a thread_local RefCell<Option<String>> that stores the full text of the most recently closed read-aloud tile (line 105 in read_aloud.rs). This text persists until a new read-aloud tile is closed or the process exits. The text can include any clipboard content the user selected for read-aloud, including potentially sensitive text. However, the data never leaves the process — it is only used to restore the tile if the user presses the restore hotkey, and it is never logged, exported, or persisted to disk.
candidates.counterevidence: The text is process-local only (thread_local), never written to disk/log, and is replaced on the next read-aloud tile close. Practical risk is minimal — an attacker with process memory access already has full application access.
candidates.remaining_check: None — confirmed but low practical impact
candidates.original_candidate_title: 4. Screen capture — no temp raw dump in this module; unbounded RAM + weak converter
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `vision_capture.rs` does not `write` BGRA to temp or `diag!` pixel payloads. The freeze lives in RAM: `capture_virtual_desktop` → `bgra_to_slint_image` (`set_frozen`) **and** `Rc` of the full `CapturedBgra` captured into persistent overlay callbacks (`on_region_selected`). That Rc is only replaced on the next F8. `bgra_to_slint_image` does `SharedPixelBuffer::new(w, h)` then copies `bgra.as_chunks::<4>()` with a `get_mut` guard; it does **not** assert `bgra.len() == w*h*4` and uses raw `fw, fh` (window size uses `.max(1)`, the image path does not). Encode is in-memory JPEG data-URL; journal stores `attached_screenshot: true` plus prompts, not the bitmap, but `PttStreamSink` seeds the convo with the data-URL.

Inspection shows restore_text_clipboard (read_aloud.rs line 27) restores the clipboard and does not log the saved content. The function correctly avoids logging sensitive clipboard data.

candidates.remaining_check: None — verification step already passed by inspection
candidates.original_candidate_title: 5. Read-aloud / clipboard — no history scrape; no scrub before store/speak/export
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `read_aloud.rs` never reads clipboard history APIs. `restore_text_clipboard` writes back a single saved UTF-8 snapshot (or clears). `spawn_text_tile` / `fill_ocr_tile` store the **full** selection/OCR string in `bridge.store_conversation` and call `speak_explicit` with no `redact_secrets`. This file only `diag!`s modifier timeout, not payload. `LAST_CLOSED_READ_TILE` retains the previous tile (and thus text) after close.

candidates.title: Archive Traversal (Tar Slip) in extract_tar_bz2
candidates.rationale: extract_tar_bz2 in download.rs (line 66-78) invokes system bsdtar with -xf/-C and NO member validation — no path safety check, no symlink/hardlink protection. In contrast, extract_zip in local_ai.rs (line 2513-2557) properly lists entries, runs archive_entry_is_safe on each (rejecting absolute paths, drive-qualified paths, and '..' traversal at line 2487-2510), THEN extracts. This confirms extract_tar_bz2 has a defense gap. However, practical exploitability requires compromising the SHA-256 pinned source (the tarball is verified by verify_sha256 at ocr_install.rs line 60 BEFORE extract_tar_bz2 is called). system_bsdtar falls back to PATH lookup only if System32 tar doesn't exist (line 87), which is a minor secondary concern.
candidates.counterevidence: SHA-256 verification occurs before extraction (ocr_install.rs line 60). Practical exploitation requires either: (1) compromising the pinned upstream asset AND updating the hash in code, or (2) TOCTOU between verify and extract. The system tar fallback to PATH (line 87) is mitigated by pinning System32\tar.exe first.
candidates.remaining_check: Confirm whether Windows bsdtar/libarchive itself rejects .. members by default (some versions do)
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `extract_tar_bz2` in `overlay-backend/src/download.rs` (`extract_tar_bz2`, `Command::new(system_bsdtar()).arg("-xf").arg(tarball).arg("-C").arg(dest_dir)`) invokes Windows `System32\tar.exe` / POSIX `tar` with **no member allow-list, no `..` / absolute-path rejection, no symlink/hardlink disable, and no post-extract containment walk**. Callers (`ocr_install.rs` `install`: `extract_tar_bz2(&tarball, &root)` into `%APPDATA%\suflyor`) trust the archive root to be `tesseract/`. A crafted `.tar.bz2` can write outside `dest_dir` (parent of `tesseract/`, Startup, other profile dirs) or plant a symlink/junction then overwrite through it. Fallback `PathBuf::from("tar.exe")` in `system_bsdtar()` also allows PATH-hijacked extractors to ignore `-C` entirely.

candidates.title: Checksum Verification TOCTOU between verify_sha256 and extract/exec
candidates.rationale: verify_sha256 reads the file by path, then extract_tar_bz2 opens the same path. A same-user process could theoretically swap the file between verify and extract. However, (1) the window is extremely narrow (milliseconds), (2) the attacker needs same-user code execution which already implies full compromise, (3) the updater hashes in-memory bytes then writes them (update.rs line 255-258), closing the download/verify gap. The report's claim is architecturally correct but practically near-impossible without prior compromise.
candidates.counterevidence: The time window between verify_sha256 and extract_tar_bz2 is effectively instantaneous in practice. The update path hashes in-memory bytes. An attacker with same-user arbitrary code execution already has full process access. TOCTOU is a theoretical concern, not a practical exploit path here.
candidates.remaining_check: None — theoretical concern acknowledged
candidates.original_claim_redacted: Integrity is bound to a **path**, not a stable fd. `verify_sha256` (`download.rs`) does `std::fs::read(path)` then returns; `ocr_install.rs` later calls `extract_tar_bz2(&tarball, &root)` on the same path. `teratts_install.rs` `install_with` does `verify_file(entry, &partial)` then `std::fs::rename(&partial, &staged)` (and resume via `verify_file` on `staged` by path). `update.rs` `download_installer` hashes **in-memory bytes** (good) then `std::fs::write(&path, &bytes)` and later `run_installer` does `Command::new(path).spawn()` with **no re-hash, no exclusive lock, no Authenticode**. Predictable locations: `%APPDATA%\suflyor\tesseract-ocr.download.tar.bz2` and `%TEMP%\suflyor-update\suflyor-slint-setup.exe`.

candidates.title: Insecure Network Protocols (curl -L redirect / reqwest redirect follow)
candidates.rationale: curl_download (download.rs line 18) checks url.trim().starts_with('https://') but passes -L to curl without --proto-redir =https or --max-redirs. A 30x redirect from the HTTPS origin could theoretically downgrade to HTTP. However: (1) the origin URLs are hardcoded GitHub/HuggingFace HTTPS addresses with SHA-256 pinned hashes, (2) the updater's is_trusted_download (update.rs line 132) is a robust allow-list, and (3) any content swap would fail the SHA-256 verification. The SSRF concern (redirect to 169.254.x.x metadata) is valid but requires MITM or compromised CDN edge — both of which indicate a much larger security failure.
candidates.counterevidence: SHA-256 verification after download prevents content compromise even if a redirect occurs. The URLs are hardcoded in source. The is_trusted_download function validates scheme, host, path, and rejects userinfo/non-standard-ports.
candidates.remaining_check: Adding --proto-redir =https to curl_download would be a defense-in-depth improvement
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `curl_download` (`download.rs`) only gates `url.trim().starts_with("https://")`, then runs `curl.exe -L --fail ... --retry-all-errors -o <dest> <url>` with **no `--proto =https`, `--proto-redir =https`, `--max-redirs`, `--proto-redir -all,https`, host allow-list, or bind/proxy restrictions**. `update.rs` `is_trusted_download` is a solid static allow-list (HTTPS, port 443, no userinfo, exact `github.com/{REPO}/` or GitHub CDN hosts), but `reqwest::Client` **follows redirects by default** after that check; CDN hosts `objects.githubusercontent.com` / `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` accept **any path**. Teratts URLs are `https://huggingface.co/...` and routinely 302 to `cdn-lfs.huggingface.co` — still via unrestricted `curl -L`.

candidates.title: Partial / Staged Downloads and Invalid Install State
candidates.rationale: ocr_install.rs removes the tarball before downloading (line 56), verifies SHA-256 (line 60), and on extract failure removes dest (line 64). The report's concern about early return via is_installed() with a partial tree is plausible but speculative — is_installed() delegates to ocr::is_available() (line 40) which checks tesseract.exe AND rus.traineddata existence. A half-unpacked archive missing either file would not pass. The updater temp file concern is even weaker: download_installer bails before writing if SHA fails (update.rs line 250).
candidates.counterevidence: OCR install removes tarball before download, verifies SHA, and cleans up on failure. The is_installed check requires specific files. The updater's hash-first-then-write pattern prevents stale installer files.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify whether files outside the tesseract/ directory could survive an extract failure
candidates.original_candidate_title: 4. Partial / Staged Downloads and Invalid Install State
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `curl_download` deletes `dest` only if curl’s **exit status** is non-success; there is no `--remove-on-error`, no fsync, no size predeclaration. Kill/crash during transfer leaves a truncated object. `ocr_install.rs` does `remove_file(&tarball)` at start (good) but **does not wipe `dest` before extract**, early-returns if `is_installed()` (resolver may treat a half-unpacked tree as ready), and on extract failure only `remove_dir_all(&dest)` — not other members dumped into `root`. Teratts is much better (`.part` → verify → rename, wipe staging on error/cancel, marker last, quarantine broken releases) but: leftover `{path}.part` after hard kill is overwritten not resumed (`curl` has no `-C -`); `check_dir` is size-only; `install` early-returns on marker + sizes without re-hashing. Updater: hash-fail bails **before** write, so a **previous** `suflyor-slint-setup.exe` in `%TEMP%\suflyor-update\` remains executable; a torn `std::fs::write` can leave a truncated MZ that still passes a naive “file exists” UI if a caller does not go through `download_installer` again.

candidates.title: Native Gate Classification Bypass — knowledge/*.md treated as docs-only
candidates.rationale: git-gate-native.ps1 line 74-76 classifies files solely by extension regex '(^|/)[^/]+\.(md|html|txt)$'. A commit touching only overlay-backend/knowledge/*.md would be classified as docs-only and skip Cargo checks entirely. The GitHub CI is-docs-only.sh (line 48) correctly handles this case by matching 'overlay-backend/knowledge/*' FIRST and returning false. This is a real asymmetry: the local native gate can be bypassed for knowledge files while GitHub CI catches it. However, the local gate is convenience enforcement — GitHub CI is the mandatory merge gate and correctly handles this.
candidates.counterevidence: GitHub CI (is-docs-only.sh line 48) correctly forces full CI for knowledge/*.md. The native gate is advisory/local enforcement only. PRs cannot merge without the CI gate job passing.
candidates.remaining_check: None — confirmed asymmetry between local and CI classifiers; CI is the binding gate
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `scripts/git-gate-native.ps1` lines 73–81 treat *any* path ending in `.md`/`.html`/`.txt` as docs-only (`$docsOnly` → `$tier = 'docs'`), then lines 147–150 **exit 0 with no Cargo/clippy/tests**. That includes `overlay-backend/knowledge/*.md`, which CI comments in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 24–32) explicitly call **code inputs that must force full CI**.

candidates.title: CI docs-only classifier allows .html/.txt to skip CI
candidates.rationale: Report claims is-docs-only.sh allows .html/.txt to skip CI. Inspecting line 49: the case pattern '*.md | docs/*' matches .md files anywhere OR anything under docs/. Standalone .html or .txt files NOT under docs/ would NOT match '*.md' and would NOT match 'docs/*', so they'd hit the '*' catch-all at line 50 and correctly trigger full CI. Only the native gate (ps1) treats .html/.txt as docs-only. The CI classifier is correct.
candidates.counterevidence: is-docs-only.sh only matches *.md (by extension) and docs/* (by path prefix). Files like scripts/foo.html would correctly fail to the catch-all.
candidates.remaining_check: None — structurally rejected
candidates.original_claim_redacted: Crate membership is only `overlay-backend/`, `slint-experiment/`, `suflyor-tts/`, `suflyor-teratts/`, `suflyor-wsola/` (lines 19–25, 67–71). On `push`, if `$tier -ne 'docs'` and `$affectedCrates` is empty, the `foreach` at lines 166–205 is a no-op and the script still prints `OK (targeted)` (lines 207–208). High-risk paths **never** select a crate: `.github/workflows/*`, `scripts/git-gate-native.ps1`, `scripts/slint-installer.nsi`, `scripts/ci.ps1`, `scripts/build-slint-release.ps1`, `deny.toml`, `.gitleaks.toml`, root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`.

candidates.title: CI inherits default permissions instead of explicit least-privilege
candidates.rationale: ci.yml and security.yml do not declare explicit top-level permissions: blocks. They rely on the repository's default permissions. While package-windows.yml correctly declares 'permissions: { contents: read }', these two workflows inherit defaults. For a public repo with Actions enabled, the default is typically read-only, but this is configuration-dependent and not explicitly locked in the workflow file.
candidates.counterevidence: GitHub's default for new repositories and public repos is read-only permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN. The workflow never needs write access. This is a best-practice hardening suggestion, not an active vulnerability.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify the repository's default workflow permissions setting

New tests not in that list never run on UI-only diffs. `clippy` is skipped entirely.

candidates.original_claim_redacted: Push base fallback (lines 42–45): if `origin/master` is missing, `$Base = 'HEAD~1'` and the diff is a **single commit**. Combined with docs-only short-circuit, a two-commit push (`feat: rust` then `docs: readme`) classifies as docs-only.

candidates.title: No Authenticode / code signing on installer or update binary
candidates.rationale: update.rs run_installer (line 262+) spawns the downloaded installer without Authenticode verification. build-slint-release.ps1 does not include any signtool.exe or code-signing step. This is a known limitation for a pre-1.0 project distributed via GitHub Releases with SHA-256 digests. The installer is NSIS-generated, per-user (no UAC), written to LOCALAPPDATA.
candidates.counterevidence: SHA-256 digest verification occurs before the installer is written (update.rs line 250). The installer runs per-user without admin privileges (NSIS installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%). SmartScreen/Defender provides OS-level unsigned binary warnings.
candidates.remaining_check: None — known pre-1.0 limitation

candidates.rationale: Report hypothesizes that gitleaks default rules may not match Groq API keys (gsk_*) or the app's bearer token format. It is the correct and intended behavior — the classifier needs git history to compute the changed file list. This is not a security finding.
candidates.counterevidence: fetch-depth:0 is required for accurate diff classification. The changes job uses it correctly. The rust and macos build jobs use default shallow checkout.

candidates.original_claim_redacted: PR title/body/branch are **not** interpolated into shell (classifier uses `env: BASE_SHA`/`HEAD_SHA`, lines 58–66) — no classic `github.event.pull_request.title` injection. Real bypass is **workflow self-rewrite + non-blocking validators**: `gate` `needs: [changes, rust]` only (lines 154–155); `macos` and `validate` are **not** required. `gate` treats `rust != true` as success (lines 168–173). A PR that sets `.github/scripts/is-docs-only.sh` to always print `true` skips the Windows rust job; if branch protection requires only `gate`, clippy/tests never run. Same PR can edit `test-docs-only-detection.sh` so `validate` also goes green.

candidates.title: Version guard does not detect NSI-only version bump without Cargo.toml
candidates.rationale: Report claims bumping only the NSI version without Cargo.toml would pass the native gate if it's classified as docs-only. However, .nsi files match the extension regex in git-gate-native.ps1 — they are NOT .md/.html/.txt, so they would be classified as targeted, triggering Cargo checks including version_guard. The report's scenario is incorrect for the native gate. However, an NSI-only bump would correctly fail version_guard (which checks Cargo.toml == NSI), making this a non-issue.
candidates.counterevidence: .nsi files don't match the docs-only pattern. A targeted gate runs cargo test which includes version_guard. The guard would catch the mismatch.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify the report's specific scenario against the actual gate classification
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `scripts/slint-installer.nsi` line 13 hardcodes `!define PRODUCT_VERSION "0.38.1-rc.3"` (also `Name`/`DisplayVersion`, lines 23, 135). `scripts/build-slint-release.ps1` invokes `makensis /V2 $nsi` (lines 148–154) with **no** `/DPRODUCT_VERSION=...` and no read of `Cargo.toml` / `Info.plist`. Native `version_guard` runs only inside `slint-experiment` tests (gate lines 181–198, and only on that crate’s targeted/full path). Changing the `.nsi` does not affect `$affectedCrates` (Finding 1), so **version_guard does not run**.
